design: Descriptive reuse of the original 12 test participants. The earlier aggregate result for the prior-stride control is already known. Freeze before fitting or viewing new outcomes. No hyperparameter search, test-based checkpoint selection, or reserve opening.
data: Katmah et al., PhysioNet multimodal gait 1.0.0, 0.5 m/s treadmill. S1-40 except S24 train; S41-52 evaluation; do not read S53-59. Verify every admitted file SHA256 and previous source member identity. Never read another speed.
eligibility: Use exactly the original eligible frame indexes, requiring finite six published angles and consecutive integer source frames from i-24 through i+15 for the legacy eligibility mask only. Also require 240 finite bilateral knee pairs at consecutive frame numbers i-239 through i. Read bilateral knees only into features. Reference is the stored right/left Xsens knee flexion/extension at i+15 in degrees. At 60 Hz the history contains four seconds of samples, spanning 239/60 seconds. Fifteen frames span 0.25 s.

output.ridge_residual: two degrees [right,left] after adding the residual to the prior stride
output.transformer_residual: two degrees [right,left] after adding the residual to the prior stride

stride: For p=45..180 inclusive, sum squared bilateral differences between the last 60 samples and the same samples p frames earlier. Choose shortest minimizing period. Forecast b=K[i+15-p].
features: For chronological offsets o=[-54,-42,-30,-21,-15,-9,-6,-3,0], concatenate nine chronological tokens of 11 fields each. For j=i+o each token is [K[j],K[j-p],K[j+15-p],K[j]-K[j-3],K[j-p]-K[j-p-3],p]. Each K is [right,left]. Ridge and Transformer receive exactly the same tokens and predict the correction Y-b. All terms are in the 240-frame prefix. No clock, person, demographics, future availability, rest of trial or other joints supplied to prediction.
normalization: Equal training-person weight. Each of the 11 features shares a mean and scale across positions, using all training cutoffs/tokens within person. Float64 moments, population variance, floor SD at 1e-6. Apply identical constants to ridge and Transformer.
ridge: Flatten normalized 9x11 in row-major order. Equal training-person weighted least squares with unpenalized intercept, ridge 0.001 on all coefficients in mean normalized covariance units. Analytic float64. Fit degree residual.
transformer: One compact encoder, width 24. Linear feature projection, learned 9x24 position embeddings (normal SD .02), 4 six-dimensional attention heads with softmax and residual, pre-LayerNorm eps 1e-5, 48-unit ReLU feedforward residual, last token LayerNorm and 2-unit affine residual output. Zero-init final readout. Bidirectional attention within an observed historical prefix; one output after that prefix. Output times 10 degrees added to b. CPU float32 training, no dropout. Smooth L1 loss (beta .3 in units of 10 degrees) against (Y-b)/10. Seed 81327 in NumPy PCG64 and PyTorch. AdamW lr .0015 weight_decay .001 default betas (.9,.999) eps 1e-8 foreach false. 1600 updates, batch 128: uniform person with replacement, then uniform eligible cutoff for each draw. Final update only.
scores: Per-person right and left mean absolute error (degrees) and bilateral mean over both knees and all eligible cutoffs. Report all twelve persons and signed paired differences candidate minus comparator; negative favors candidate. Equal person mean. For ridge vs stride, transformer vs stride, transformer vs ridge, publish wins/ties/losses and 95% paired percentile intervals from 10000 participant-level resamples of 12 with replacement, NumPy PCG64 seed 21301. Intervals are descriptive and unadjusted. Report all losses and ties. Reference prior-stride mean 3.5352540464780127 degrees and 40201 cutoffs on S41-52 must match within 1e-8 degree and exactly, respectively.
criteria: For descriptive support on a particular comparator require mean signed difference below zero, upper bootstrap bound below zero and lower MAE in at least 8 of 12 participants. Transformer advantage requires passing against both rule and ridge. Otherwise explicitly report the failed comparison. Any superiority on this previously examined cohort still requires prospective confirmation elsewhere.
controls: Verify original per-person stride MAE and counts, exact cohort hashes and frame eligibility. Check portable versus PyTorch predictions within 0.001 degree. Change future values after a cutoff: prediction and period must remain identical while target changes. Scalar phase search and direct cutoff indexing must match optimized features. Invented histories only in public examples. No release of raw participant angle sequences.
compute: Cap training inter-op/BLAS at one. Compare one versus two intra-op CPU threads using S1-only 20-update probes and retain the faster end-to-end accurate probe. No probe checkpoint enters the full fit. CPU-only PyTorch and NumPy control vector/kernel scheduling. Freeze fitted weights before evaluation. Report actual route and times.
